appearance.bark_look.note: Poplar bark: shoots with dash lenticels, and trunks furrowed into long flat ridges as they age (cottonwoods all over; aspens at the base, their species adding their smooth white stage). Reference: quaking aspen's record (plantgen-claude project-files/bark/records/populus-tremuloides.json); the genus furrows as the aspen's base does, inferred.

traits.short_shoots.note: Hallé, Oldeman and Tomlinson 1978, p. 60: short shoots live a limited time and often fall cleanly at a scar, as in Populus.

traits.perianth.note: Ronse De Craene, Floral Diagrams (2010) p. 257: Salix and Populus are the extreme of the family's floral reduction, their flowers in catkins with no perianth (nectar glands in its place in Salix).
